---
title: "The Roads"
subtitle: "Question 4 — Collision risk"
---

The question this section was meant to answer is where pumas are killed by
vehicles. That question cannot be answered here yet, because the data that would
answer it are not in hand. So this section does two things instead: it states
what is missing, and it presents the best interim proxy — where the corridor and 
dangerous roads coincide.

## What is missing?

Direct roadkill records for the Bay Area are held in the California Roadkill
Observation System (CROS), maintained by the UC Davis Road Ecology Center. A data
request has been made with data pending. The project does not scrape or reconstruct those records —
they are used with authorisation. Until the data has been shared, there is **no
published mortality-point layer in this project**. When the CROS records are available, 
they will overlay the risk surface below as a validation layer — confirming or correcting where the proxy points.

## The interim proxy — where traffic meets the corridor

What the analysis *can* say comes from combining two things: how
busy each road is (traffic volume, from the crossing analysis in the connectivity
section) and whether that road sits inside the **core** corridor, where a puma is
most likely to actually move. Collision risk is highest where both are true.

The connectivity section ranked road
crossings by traffic, and several busy roads appeared near the top. But most of
those busy roads clip the corridor at its permeable edges, not through its core.
When the core-corridor filter is applied, the risk narrows sharply.

```{r}
#| label: fig-puma-risk
#| fig-alt: "Zoomed south-Bay map of road crossings, those inside the core corridor coloured blue to magenta by traffic and those outside greyed, with US-101 at Coyote Valley standing out as high-traffic inside the corridor."
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Collision-risk proxy: road crossings where traffic and the core corridor coincide. Crossings inside the core corridor are coloured by traffic volume (blue for quiet to magenta for busy); crossings outside the core are greyed — they are barriers, but not where a puma is most likely to cross. US-101 at Coyote Valley is the one crossing that is both high-traffic and inside the core corridor, which makes it the clear top collision risk."

library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(dplyr)

cr <- st_read("../data/processed/lcp_puma_scmtns_to_diablo_crossings_3310.gpkg",
              quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(4326)

# In-core crossings carry the risk story; out-of-core are context (greyed).
cr$core <- cr$in_core == 1 | cr$in_core == TRUE
in_core  <- cr[cr$core, ]
out_core <- cr[!cr$core, ]

# Core swath band underneath — the corridor the risk is measured against.
core_ctx <- st_read("../data/processed/lcp_puma_scmtns_to_diablo_swath_3310.gpkg",
                    quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(4326)
core_ctx <- core_ctx[core_ctx$tier == "core", ]

pal <- colorNumeric(c("#3b8bc2", "#5e4fa2", "#8c2d8f", "#c31d6b"),
                    domain = c(0, max(cr$aadt, na.rm = TRUE)))
in_core$wt <- 2.5 + 4.5 * sqrt(in_core$aadt / max(cr$aadt, na.rm = TRUE))

leaflet(options = leafletOptions(minZoom = 6, zoomSnap = 0.1)) |>
  addTiles(
    urlTemplate = "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Canvas/World_Light_Gray_Base/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
    attribution = "Tiles &copy; Esri"
  ) |>
  # road overlay: grey roads + labels on the neutral base, no relief/colour
  addTiles(
    urlTemplate = "https://services.arcgisonline.com/arcgis/rest/services/Reference/World_Transportation/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
    attribution = "Roads &copy; Esri, HERE, Garmin, &copy; OpenStreetMap contributors"
  ) |>
  # core corridor band underneath
  addPolygons(
    data = core_ctx,
    fillColor = "#7d3f16", fillOpacity = 0.15,
    color = "#7d3f16", weight = 0.8, opacity = 0.4,
    label = "Core corridor (risk measured against this zone)"
  ) |>
  # out-of-core crossings — greyed context, thin
  addPolylines(
    data = out_core,
    color = "#9aa0a6", weight = 1.5, opacity = 0.6,
    label = ~sprintf("%s — %s AADT — outside core (barrier, lower crossing risk)",
                     road_label, format(round(aadt), big.mark = ","))
  ) |>
  # in-core crossings — the risk-relevant ones, coloured by traffic
  addPolylines(
    data = in_core,
    color = ~pal(aadt), weight = ~wt, opacity = 0.95,
    label = ~sprintf("%s — %s AADT — IN core corridor",
                     road_label, format(round(aadt), big.mark = ",")),
    popup = ~sprintf("<b>%s</b><br>%s vehicles/day<br>Inside core corridor<br>Barrier rank %d of 290",
                     road_label, format(round(aadt), big.mark = ","), rank_overall)
  ) |>
  addControl(
    position = "bottomleft",
    html = htmltools::HTML(
      "<div style='background:#fff;padding:8px 10px;border-radius:4px;
                   box-shadow:0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.2);font-size:12px;
                   line-height:1.4;text-align:left;max-width:215px;'>
         <div style='font-weight:600;margin-bottom:5px;'>Collision-risk proxy</div>
         <div style='height:12px;border-radius:2px;margin-bottom:3px;
                     background:linear-gradient(to right,#3b8bc2,#5e4fa2,#8c2d8f,#c31d6b);'></div>
         <div style='display:flex;justify-content:space-between;margin-bottom:5px;'>
           <span>quiet</span><span>busy (AADT)</span></div>
         <div style='display:flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;'>
           <span style='width:20px;border-top:2.5px solid #9aa0a6;display:inline-block;'></span>outside core (context)</div>
         <div style='margin-top:5px;color:#5a6070;font-size:11px;'>
           Coloured = busy road inside the core corridor = higher risk. Proxy, not mortality counts. No puma locations shown.</div>
       </div>"
    )
  ) |>
  # Responsive fit (ported from landscape.qmd): waits for the container to have a
  # real height before fitting, so fitBounds never runs against a 0-height box.
  # zoomSnap on the map lets the fit land fractionally and adapt to frame width.
  # Debounced ResizeObserver re-fits on later resizes (phone reflow, orientation).
  htmlwidgets::onRender("
    function(el, x) {
      var map = this;
      var bounds = [[37.01977, -122.17587], [37.28626, -121.69144]];   // [[S,W],[N,E]] this map's extent
      function doFit() {
        map.invalidateSize();
        var pad = window.innerWidth <= 760 ? [30, 30] : [55, 55];
        map.fitBounds(bounds, { padding: pad });
      }
      var tries = 0;
      function fitWhenReady() {
        if (el.clientHeight > 50 && el.clientWidth > 50) {
          doFit();
        } else if (tries++ < 60) {
          requestAnimationFrame(fitWhenReady);
        }
      }
      fitWhenReady();
      var rafId = null;
      if (window.ResizeObserver) {
        var ro = new ResizeObserver(function() {
          if (rafId) cancelAnimationFrame(rafId);
          rafId = requestAnimationFrame(doFit);
        });
        ro.observe(el);
      }
      window.addEventListener('orientationchange', doFit);
    }
  ")
```

The map makes the filter visible. Most of the busy roads the corridor crosses are
grey, because they clip the corridor outside its core. What is coloured — busy
*and* in the core — is dominated by one road: **US-101 at Coyote Valley.** It is
the single crossing that is both high-traffic and inside the core corridor, and so
it is the clear top collision-risk location, not merely the top barrier.

## The risk ranking

Ranking the crossings by the two factors together — traffic volume and
core-corridor membership — puts US-101 alone at the top. The next-busiest roads
fall away because they sit outside the core; the other in-core roads are quiet.

| Road | Traffic (AADT) | In core corridor | Barrier rank |
|------|---------------:|:----------------:|:------------:|
| US-101 (Coyote Valley) | 142,000 | Yes | 1 |
| Santa Cruz Highway | 64,900 | No | 8 |
| Route 17 | 60,200 | No | 28 |
| Big Basin Way | 7,200 | Yes | 62 |
| Summit Road | 1,050 | Yes | 69 |

: Top road crossings by traffic and core-corridor overlap. Only US-101 is both
high-traffic and in-core — the combination that defines collision risk. Traffic
values are directly measured; see the connectivity section for the full
confidence-tiered ranking. {.striped}

The result: **one road
carries most of the corridor's collision risk.** Santa Cruz Highway and Route 17
are busy, but the corridor crosses them at its edges, not its core. Big Basin Way
and Summit Road are in the core, but they are quiet mountain roads. US-101 is the
only place where heavy traffic and the core corridor meet.
